newsitem.title: USA: Excite updates WebCrawler search service.
newsitem.headline: Excite updates WebCrawler search service.

text.p: Excite Inc. said it will Monday launch a new version of WebCrawler, the Internet search site it acquired from America Online when AOL took a stake in Excite last year.
The new version, dubbed WebCrawler 3.0, aims to further simplify the process of finding information on the World Wide Web for consumers who have been its primary focus since WebCrawler's inception.
Among the new features is WebCrawler Shortcuts, a new searching capability the company said will deliver information about relevant resources and recommendations along with search results.

With a new look, the search engine is designed to provide uncluttered links to relevant Web sites, and the shortcut feature provides opportunities for advertisers to promote their services beyond traditional banner ads.
Excite said Classifieds 2000, N2K's Music Boulevard, MapQuest, DejaNews and WhoWhere?
An initial promotional contest will award prizes of frequent flyer miles on AMR Corp.'s American Airlines and United Airlines to the winners.

Last week Excite rolled out a new feature on its main Excite search page which simplifies the process of entering a detailed search, including the option of using automated wizards to help users complete their search.

Also last week, financial services and software company Intuit Inc. agreed to invest $40 million for a 19 percent stake in Excite in a deal which also included a seven year contract to establish an Intuit financial area, or channel, available through Excite. (sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau 415 846 5400)
